name: Oluwaseun Adebanjo
headline: Senior Platform Engineer
summary: Senior platform engineer with twelve years in infrastructure, the last six building internal platforms on AWS. I care about golden paths that let product teams ship without filing tickets. Most of my time goes to EKS clusters, Pulumi programs and GitOps workflows, with a strong interest in cost visibility and developer experience. Outside work I run a small study group for engineers preparing cloud certifications and contribute documentation fixes to open-source tools I rely on.

bullets: Run a fleet of nine EKS clusters serving 140 microservices; cut node spend by 31% through bin-packing and spot capacity.
Replaced hand-built environments with Pulumi stacks written in TypeScript, shrinking new-environment lead time from two weeks to forty minutes.
Introduced ArgoCD and a GitOps repository layout; deployments went from weekly to roughly 60 a day with automated rollback on failed health checks.
Mentor four engineers and chair the platform guild.
Defined a cost-allocation tagging scheme and a weekly report so every squad sees what its workloads cost.
Partnered with the security team on admission rules, image signing and short-lived credentials for all clusters.
Containerised a monolithic e-commerce stack and moved it from bare-metal hosts to a managed container service.
Wrote Jenkins shared libraries used by 30 teams for build, scan and release automation.
Built the first on-call rota and runbooks; mean time to recovery fell from 95 to 22 minutes.
Taught developers to read dashboards and trace requests, which reduced escalations to the infrastructure team by about a quarter.
Piloted service mesh traffic shifting for safer releases of the checkout service.
Looked after 400 Linux servers, patching, monitoring with Nagios and scripting routine work in Bash and Python.
Automated provisioning with Puppet, removing most manual server builds.
Built a small internal wiki of recurring fixes that cut repeat tickets noticeably.

name: Fionnuala Brannigan
headline: Site Reliability Engineer
summary: SRE focused on reliability targets, observability and boring, repeatable operations. I have spent eight years moving teams from heroics to SLOs. Day to day I work on GKE, OpenTofu modules and GitLab pipelines, and I enjoy writing blameless postmortems more than I probably should. I am equally comfortable in front of a dashboard at 3am and in a room explaining reliability trade-offs to product managers, and I mentor junior engineers on incident response.

bullets: Defined SLOs for 25 customer-facing services and introduced error-budget reviews that cut paging noise by 45%.
Maintain the GKE estate (autopilot and standard) and a library of OpenTofu modules shared across six squads.
Own the GitLab CI templates that build, scan, sign and promote container images to production.
Led a zero-downtime migration of the primary database to a regional replica topology.
Introduced load-testing before major launches; found a connection pool limit that would have caused an outage during the spring promotion.
Wrote the incident response playbook, with clear roles for commander, scribe and communications lead.
Managed VM fleets on GCP and later moved workloads to GKE with Helm charts.
Built reusable infrastructure-as-code modules for networks and IAM, later ported to OpenTofu.
Set up centralised logging and dashboards that the support team still uses.
Reduced alert volume by consolidating 300 rules into 90 symptom-based ones.
Trained eight developers to carry their own pager for the services they own.
Handled tickets, patching and backups for managed hosting customers.
Wrote monitoring checks and a first set of Ansible playbooks.
Wrote Python scripts that checked backup integrity and reported failures to chat.

name: Tomasz Wierzbicki
headline: DevOps Engineer
summary: DevOps engineer, nine years in on-premises and hybrid environments. I automate whatever a team does twice. Strongest with Jenkins, Ansible and OpenShift; comfortable reading other people's legacy scripts and gradually replacing them with something testable. My preference is for simple, observable automation that new colleagues can understand on their first day, and I regularly present lunch-and-learn sessions on shell scripting, containers and secure defaults for the wider IT department.

bullets: Operate the OpenShift platform (three clusters, about 70 namespaces) and onboard development teams.
Maintain 120 Jenkins pipelines; introduced pipeline-as-code and cut average build time by a third.
Wrote Ansible roles for hardening and patching 300 RHEL hosts, passing two external audits without findings.
Integrated HashiCorp Vault for secrets, removing credentials from repositories.
Created a shared base image catalogue, patched monthly, which removed dozens of vulnerable images from production.
Defined naming and tagging conventions for projects and routes so billing and ownership are always clear.
Managed release calendars for a billing platform, with manual deployments gradually replaced by scripted ones.
Set up Nexus and SonarQube and enforced quality gates before artefacts could be promoted.
Trained developers on Git branching and code review.
Reduced release windows from four hours to forty minutes by scripting database migration checks and smoke tests.
Maintained a change log that auditors praised as the clearest they had seen.
Administered Linux servers, Apache and Tomcat stacks.
Wrote Bash tooling for backups and log rotation.
Learned to monitor everything with Zabbix and to document alerts properly.

name: Priyanka Venkataraghavan
headline: Cloud Engineer
summary: Cloud engineer working on Azure for seven years. I design landing zones, write Bicep, and look after AKS workloads for a banking client. I like clear documentation, tagging standards and anything that makes audits easier. I enjoy working with security and finance colleagues to balance control and speed, and I volunteer as a mentor in a women-in-technology programme that supports early-career engineers in Bengaluru.

bullets: Built a multi-subscription landing zone with management groups, policy guardrails and hub-and-spoke networking, all in Bicep.
Operate AKS clusters hosting 35 workloads; handled version upgrades with no customer-visible downtime.
Authored Azure DevOps release pipelines with approval gates, vulnerability scanning and automated smoke tests.
Reduced idle cloud cost by 22% with schedule-based scaling and right-sizing reports.
Implemented private endpoints, managed identities and key vault integration across production workloads.
Prepared quarterly cost and compliance reports for the risk committee, based on policy compliance data.
Run monthly game-day exercises with application owners to rehearse failover between regions and refine recovery runbooks.
Coordinate with the security operations centre on alert tuning so only actionable findings reach the on-call engineer.
Migrated 60 virtual machines from a private data centre to Azure IaaS.
Scripted resource deployment with ARM templates and PowerShell.
Supported three client teams during weekend cutovers.
Documented a repeatable migration approach, including dependency mapping and rollback plans.
Trained the support team on Azure Monitor alerts and runbook automation.
Prepared training material and hands-on labs that onboarded twelve new consultants to the Azure estate within a quarter.

name: Lars Ostergaard-Weiss
headline: Infrastructure Engineer
summary: Infrastructure engineer, five years of experience, mostly on AWS with CloudFormation and Helm. Quiet but thorough. I like small pull requests, good dashboards and sleeping through the night. Outside of work I maintain a small open-source tool for tidying unused AWS resources, and I like cycling to the office whenever the Danish weather allows.

bullets: Own the AWS accounts for a SaaS product with 90 employees; every resource is defined in CloudFormation or CDK.
Deploy workloads to EKS using Helm charts and GitHub Actions workflows with environment protection rules.
Introduced Datadog monitors tied to service ownership, reducing unowned alerts to zero.
Ran the migration from a single shared account to separate accounts per environment.
Created a reusable template for new services covering load balancer, autoscaling, alarms and dashboards, now used by all teams.
Rotated all long-lived access keys to short-lived roles via federation.
Review pull requests from developers who change infrastructure, offering guidance on least privilege and sensible defaults.
Schedule quarterly disaster recovery rehearsals and publish short summaries of what we learned and what we will change.
Maintained build servers and moved nightly builds to hosted runners.
Wrote Python scripts for AWS cost reports and unused-resource clean-up.
Took part in the on-call rota with a senior colleague.
Wrote runbooks for the five most common incidents and used them to train two new colleagues.
Reduced hosted runner minutes by 35% with smarter caching and path filters.
Participated in architecture reviews and helped choose managed services instead of self-hosted components where it reduced maintenance.

name: Chidinma Okwuosa
headline: Junior DevOps Engineer
summary: Two years into my career after a bootcamp and a computer science degree. I support the infrastructure team with deployments, monitoring and documentation, and I am learning cluster operations and infrastructure as code from excellent mentors. I document what I learn on a personal blog, mentor secondary school students in a coding club on weekends, and keep a home lab where I practise cluster failures and recovery.

bullets: Maintain GitHub Actions workflows for five services, adding caching that made builds about 40% faster.
Help operate a small Kubernetes cluster on a managed cloud service; handle routine upgrades and certificate renewals under supervision.
Wrote Ansible playbooks to configure Nginx and monitoring agents on 25 virtual machines.
Keep runbooks current and join the on-call rota as secondary responder.
Created an onboarding checklist and a glossary for new team members, which cut first-week questions significantly.
Set up uptime checks and Grafana panels for the customer-facing API and shared the results at the weekly meeting.
Pair weekly with a senior engineer to review incidents, read logs together and practise safe rollbacks in a staging environment.
Contribute small fixes to internal tooling, including a script that rotates log files and alerts when disks reach 80% usage.
Resolved internal tickets, set up laptops and managed user accounts.
Automated a weekly disk-usage report with a Bash script that the team now uses every Monday.
Learned the company's deployment process in three weeks and was trusted with production releases by month five.
Completed an internal training programme on Linux fundamentals, networking and basic security hygiene, finishing at the top of the cohort.

name: Callum Pettigrew
headline: Senior Site Reliability Engineer
summary: I have spent fourteen years keeping production systems alive, first as a sysadmin, then as a DevOps engineer and now as an SRE at a streaming business. My toolbox these days: AKS, Pulumi in Python, ArgoCD, Azure Pipelines and a lot of Grafana. Away from the keyboard I am a volunteer lifeboat crew member, which has taught me more about calm leadership under pressure than any course.

bullets: Responsible for the availability of a video delivery platform peaking at 2.3 million concurrent viewers; delivered 99.95% over the last four years.
Operate AKS node pools with KEDA autoscaling for bursty encoding jobs, saving roughly 180,000 pounds a year.
Describe all cloud resources in Pulumi (Python) and review every change through pull requests.
Run quarterly game days and chaos experiments; found and fixed eleven hidden single points of failure.
Interview and onboard new SREs.
Wrote a capacity model that predicts encoding demand from the release calendar and has been within 6% for two years.
Cut mean time to detect from 11 minutes to under 3 through better symptom-based alerts and synthetic probes.
Brought the build, test and release process of four game backends into one set of pipelines in Jenkins and later Azure DevOps.
Containerised services and introduced rolling deployments on a container orchestration platform.
Implemented central metrics collection and alert routing.
Created self-service tooling that lets developers create test environments on demand and tear them down automatically.
Presented the migration case study at two regional conferences.
Supported 800 users and 60 Windows and Linux servers.
Managed VMware hosts, backups and a small Cisco network.
Learned to write clear incident reports and to keep calm on the phone with angry users.

name: Ananya Raghunathan
headline: Platform Engineer
summary: Platform engineer building internal developer tooling. I treat the platform as a product: user research, roadmaps and measured adoption. Technically I work with Crossplane, Backstage, GKE and Tekton, and I like pairing with application teams to remove friction. I write regularly on the engineering blog, give talks at the local platform meetup in Pune, and mentor two junior colleagues who are moving from application development into infrastructure.

bullets: Launched a Backstage-based developer portal with software templates; new services now reach production in two days instead of three weeks.
Provide self-service databases and queues through Crossplane compositions on GCP.
Operate GKE clusters managed with Flux, with admission policies written in Open Policy Agent.
Run monthly developer surveys; satisfaction score rose from 6.1 to 8.4.
Established a service catalogue with ownership metadata, which allowed incident responders to find the right team in seconds.
Introduced golden-path templates for APIs, workers and scheduled jobs, with security scanning built in.
Pair with application teams during their first deployments to understand where the platform confuses people, then fix the root cause.
Publish a quarterly platform roadmap and changelog so teams can plan around deprecations and new capabilities.
Wrote command-line tools in Go for the internal support team.
Maintained Tekton pipelines for twelve repositories.
Documented onboarding steps and recorded short training videos.
Added cost visibility in the portal so that teams can see monthly spend per service.
Rolled out a deprecation process for old tooling with clear dates and migration guides.
Ran internal workshops on declarative configuration and on reading cluster events when something goes wrong.

certifications: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer

name: Dieter Hollenbeck
headline: Systems Engineer
summary: Systems engineer for sixteen years, with a steady move from physical servers to software-defined infrastructure. Currently I design and run a private cloud on OpenStack with Ansible, Nomad and Consul for a manufacturer. Pragmatic, security-minded and fond of reproducible builds. I am a long-time contributor on a regional Linux user group and maintain a handful of Ansible roles that I have published for others to reuse.

bullets: Run a private cloud with 1,200 vCPUs for plant analytics, supporting 14 internal teams.
Automate every host with Ansible and Packer images; a full rebuild of the control plane takes under two hours.
Schedule workloads with Nomad and Consul service discovery; roll out new versions with canary releases from GitLab CI.
Led the hardening effort for an ISO 27001 audit.
Replaced manual quarterly patching with scheduled, rolling maintenance that never drops production lines.
Implemented WireGuard tunnels for secure connections between the plants and the central private cloud.
Maintain a documented disaster recovery plan, including offline copies of configuration, keys and images stored in a separate fire zone.
Coordinate with plant electricians on power and cooling upgrades for the server rooms.
Operated KVM virtualisation clusters and Ceph storage.
Introduced configuration management with Puppet, later Ansible.
Built monitoring around Nagios and subsequently Prometheus.
Built an image pipeline with Packer, producing signed golden images every week.
Set up Prometheus federation across three sites with alert routing by ownership.
Rolled out centralised logging with Loki and a small set of dashboards used by the factory support desk.
Maintained Linux and Windows servers, mail and backups for 120 staff.
Gained deep experience with RAID, backup and disaster recovery on commodity hardware.

name: Marisol Quintanilla-Ruiz
headline: Cloud Engineer
summary: Cloud engineer with six years on Google Cloud. I build secure, cost-aware environments for data and web teams. Fan of Cloud Run, Config Connector and tidy IAM. I speak at local meetups about FinOps. Beyond engineering I coordinate a monthly FinOps meetup in Madrid and enjoy translating cloud pricing into language that finance teams find useful.

bullets: Designed the organisation hierarchy, networking and IAM model for 40 GCP projects.
Provision infrastructure declaratively with Config Connector and reusable blueprints.
Moved 18 stateless services to Cloud Run with Cloud Build triggers, shortening release cycles from days to hours.
Cut monthly spend by 28% through committed use discounts, labels and weekly cost reviews.
Implemented organisation policies that block public buckets and enforce regional restrictions.
Introduced a landing-zone checklist and baseline for every new project so that security reviews take hours, not weeks.
Introduced budgets and alerts per project, plus weekly anomaly notifications that caught a runaway query costing several thousand euros.
Run quarterly access reviews and remove unused service accounts and permissions.
Run a monthly review with data teams to retire unused datasets, buckets and idle clusters, reporting savings to engineering managers.
Supported customers migrating workloads to GCP.
Prepared Deployment Manager templates and migration checklists.
Handled first-line incidents for cloud customers.
Built a cost dashboard in BigQuery for engineering managers, which led to three major clean-up campaigns.
Mentored two graduate engineers during their first year.
Prepared workshops for customers on identity, networking and cost control on Google Cloud, attended by around 60 people.

name: Bartholomew Achterberg
headline: Staff Platform Engineer
summary: Staff platform engineer with seventeen years in infrastructure. I set technical direction for a platform group of 22 people and still write code weekly. Kubernetes, Terraform and CI/CD are the core of what we provide; reliability, security and cost are what we are judged on. I spend as much time on people and priorities as on code: hiring, writing design documents and saying no to shiny things that would not help our users. I speak regularly at European infrastructure conferences.

bullets: Architected a multi-region Kubernetes platform running 600 services and 4,000 pods at peak.
Maintain 300 Terraform modules with automated testing and a registry that every team consumes.
Designed the company-wide CI/CD standard, reducing median lead time for change from nine days to under four hours.
Drove the adoption of Cilium and eBPF-based observability.
Coach senior engineers and write the platform roadmap.
Defined the on-call policy and training path, reducing out-of-hours pages per engineer by 60% over two years.
Negotiated cloud commitments with finance and saved roughly 1.2 million euros annually.
Led the move from data-centre hosting to AWS for a travel booking site.
Introduced Terraform and replaced manual change tickets with reviewed pull requests.
Built early Docker-based deployment tooling.
Mentored three engineers into senior roles.
Built a deployment dashboard showing lead time, change failure rate and recovery time per team.
Ran shared hosting and virtual private servers on Linux.
Automated provisioning with Puppet and Bash.
Learned the value of boring technology and written runbooks.

name: Siobhan Gallagher-Doyle
headline: DevOps Engineer
summary: DevOps engineer, eight years. Hands-on with Terraform, Kubernetes and CI/CD for a healthcare software company, where compliance matters as much as speed. I like clear change records and fast feedback loops. I enjoy working with clinical and compliance colleagues, translating requirements into controls that engineers can actually follow, and I take pride in audit-ready, well-documented systems.

bullets: Provision Azure environments with Terraform and keep state in locked, versioned storage.
Run Kubernetes workloads for a patient scheduling product; zero unplanned downtime in the last 18 months.
Standardised CI/CD workflows in GitHub Actions with static analysis, container scanning and signed releases.
Prepare evidence for HIPAA-style and ISO audits straight from pipeline logs.
Introduced secret scanning, dependency checks and branch protection across 60 repositories.
Implemented encrypted backups and disaster recovery tests twice a year, meeting a four-hour recovery objective.
Run quarterly disaster recovery exercises and record recovery times against agreed objectives.
Work with the data protection officer to map technical controls to regulatory requirements and keep the mapping current.
Provide guidance to developers on safe configuration of cloud storage, network rules and access roles, with clear examples in the wiki.
Handle on-call escalations for the scheduling product one week in four, with documented handovers.
Maintained Jenkins build farm and artefact storage.
Introduced automated regression runs that ran on every merge.
Supported 40 developers across three offices.
Reduced pipeline time from 35 to 14 minutes with caching, parallel jobs and selective test runs.
Mentored two apprentices.
Wrote scripts that generate environment inventories and flag drift between declared and actual configuration.

name: Emeka Nwankwo-Lindqvist
headline: Site Reliability Engineer
summary: SRE with ten years of experience across Nigeria and Sweden. I focus on resilience, capacity planning and incident response for payment systems. Kubernetes and Terraform are daily tools; I write most of my automation in Go. I am comfortable with Swedish and English documentation and bridge teams across Nigeria and Sweden, and I enjoy sharing lessons about resilient payment systems at industry meetups.

bullets: Own reliability of the card authorisation path handling 1,500 transactions per second.
Operate Kubernetes clusters in two regions with Terraform-managed networking and node groups.
Maintain CI/CD pipelines with progressive delivery and automatic rollback.
Led 30 incident reviews and drove the action items to closure.
Introduced chaos drills against the authorisation path to prove failover works before peak season.
Wrote capacity forecasts based on seasonal traffic; Black Friday ran without manual intervention for the first time.
Define and track service level objectives with product owners, and report monthly on reliability, latency and error budgets.
Coordinate with the security team on certificate rotation, key management and audit evidence for payment standards.
Automated deployment of e-commerce services and monitoring.
Introduced centralised logging with the ELK stack.
Wrote a Go service that reconciled payment status across providers.
Implemented distributed tracing across 40 services to find latency hotspots.
Trained support analysts to read dashboards and triage alerts.
Maintained Linux hosts, load balancers and database replicas, and handled capacity requests during shopping peaks.
Administered Linux servers and branch networks for an ISP.
Learned about operating in constrained networks, which shaped my interest in resilience.

name: Gareth Penhaligon
headline: Cloud Engineer
summary: Cloud engineer in my third year, working on Terraform and Kubernetes for a small agency. I enjoy learning, writing things down and pairing with senior colleagues. Currently studying for the CKA. I am quick to ask for help, keen to take on on-call responsibilities as I grow, and I run a small home lab where I rebuild clusters from scratch every few weekends to practise recovery.

bullets: Manage AWS accounts for 12 client websites with Terraform modules I helped create.
Deploy client applications to a shared Kubernetes cluster and handle routine upgrades.
Maintain CI/CD pipelines in GitLab, including preview environments for every merge request.
Produce monthly uptime and cost summaries for account managers.
Wrote documentation and short screencasts so account managers can request new environments without engineering help.
Added automated TLS certificate renewals and expiry alerts, eliminating certificate incidents.
Review upgrade notes for new versions before every change, and test upgrades in a copy of the cluster before touching production.
Collaborate with front-end developers to speed up deployments of static sites using cached builds and a content delivery network.
Keep a personal learning log and share one new technique with the team every fortnight.
Support a small team of three developers and one designer, joining stand-ups and helping estimate infrastructure work.
Answered hosting tickets, restored backups and debugged slow WordPress sites.
Wrote shell scripts for repetitive customer requests.
Helped migrate three WordPress clients to containers with managed databases.
Wrote clear, step-by-step answers for customers and learned to prioritise urgent incidents calmly.
Took part in weekend maintenance work with senior colleagues and practised safe rollbacks.

name: Kavitha Subramaniam
headline: Infrastructure Engineer
summary: Infrastructure engineer, eleven years, specialising in reliable hybrid environments for financial services. I work with Terraform, Kubernetes and Jenkins CI/CD, and I am happiest when change is boring. I lead by writing things down, running blameless reviews and keeping change small, and I have mentored a number of junior engineers who have since moved into cloud roles at other firms.

bullets: Lead a team of five running hybrid infrastructure across two data centres and AWS.
Codify networks, security groups and clusters in Terraform with peer-reviewed plans.
Operate on-premises Kubernetes for trading analytics; capacity planning keeps utilisation at 70%.
Standardise CI/CD on Jenkins with approval gates required for regulated systems.
Reduced unplanned outages by 40% over three years through patch automation, capacity reviews and failover testing.
Documented infrastructure standards used as the basis for the firm's regulatory resilience submissions.
Chair the weekly change advisory meeting and review risks, rollback plans and test evidence for each submitted change.
Coordinate capacity planning with business units twice a year using utilisation trends and growth forecasts.
Managed VMware and storage for 300 hosts.
Introduced Ansible for patching and compliance checks.
Handled incident escalations on a 24x7 rota.
Planned and executed a data centre exit for two environments over a single weekend.
Reviewed vendor contracts and negotiated better support terms.
Maintained detailed runbooks for storage, network and virtualisation failures, and ran incident drills with the operations team.
Supported ERP servers and database backups.
Learned a great deal about change control in regulated settings.

name: Jasper Vandenbroucke
headline: Platform Engineer
summary: Platform engineer who came over from backend development. Four years building paved roads: Kubernetes, Terraform and CI/CD templates that other teams can adopt in an afternoon. I still enjoy writing Java when the platform needs a custom controller. In my spare time I contribute to a small open-source Kubernetes operator project and mentor developers who want to learn more about infrastructure.

bullets: Build and maintain the internal Kubernetes platform used by 15 product teams.
Provide reusable Terraform modules and CI/CD templates; adoption reached 90% of services in a year.
Wrote a Kotlin operator that automates namespace creation, quotas and network policies.
Support teams during onboarding through office hours and short workshops.
Introduced policy checks in pipelines to enforce resource limits, labels and image provenance.
Improved cluster costs by 25% by right-sizing node pools and introducing autoscaling.
Maintain a documentation site with tutorials, reference pages and a changelog, reviewed by product teams every quarter.
Run a fortnightly office hour where teams bring problems, and track recurring questions to decide what to automate next.
Investigate production incidents together with developers and propose platform improvements that prevent a repeat.
Developed Java services for a logistics API.
Started the first Docker-based deployments and pipelines for the team.
Wrote integration tests and improved build times.
Reduced average build time by 40% with caching and a modular build structure.
Learned how to design for both developers and operators through close collaboration with colleagues.
Designed REST endpoints and background workers in Java, with attention to timeouts, retries and graceful shutdown.
Participated in code reviews and wrote migration scripts for relational databases.

name: Duarte Calheiros Brandão
headline: Engenheiro DevOps
summary: Engenheiro DevOps com nove anos de experiência, sobretudo em ambientes de banca e seguros. Trabalho com OpenShift, Ansible e Jenkins, e gosto de transformar processos manuais em automatização fiável. Sou pragmático, documento tudo e procuro reduzir o risco em cada alteração. Fora do trabalho organizo encontros mensais de DevOps em Braga e dou formação interna a programadores sobre contentores, segredos e boas práticas de entrega.

bullets: Gestão de dois clusters OpenShift com cerca de 50 aplicações; as atualizações passaram a ser feitas sem paragem de serviço.
Mantenho pipelines em Jenkins e ArgoCD para entrega contínua, com testes automáticos e aprovações por ambiente.
Escrevi roles de Ansible para configurar e proteger 200 servidores, o que reduziu o tempo de preparação de um dia para uma hora.
Introduzi o Vault para gestão de segredos.
Criação de um catálogo de imagens base atualizadas todos os meses, o que reduziu vulnerabilidades críticas em produção.
Definição de normas de nomes e etiquetas para projetos, facilitando a faturação e a identificação de responsáveis.
Administração de servidores Linux e AIX para sistemas de pagamentos.
Automatização de rotinas de deploy com scripts Bash e Ansible.
Participação na escala de piquete e na resolução de incidentes críticos.
Documentação de todos os procedimentos de recuperação de desastre e realização de testes semestrais.
Redução do tempo de lançamento de quatro horas para quarenta minutos através de verificações automáticas.
Suporte a servidores e redes de clientes empresariais.
Instalação e monitorização de máquinas virtuais.
Aprendizagem profunda de Linux, redes e armazenamento em ambiente crítico.

certifications: Red Hat Certified Specialist in OpenShift

name: Larissa Fontenele Albuquerque
headline: Engenheira de Plataforma
summary: Engenheira de plataforma com sete anos de experiência em produtos digitais. Constrói e opera plataformas internas para equipas de desenvolvimento, com foco em experiência do programador, segurança e custos. Trabalho diariamente com EKS, Pulumi, GitOps e GitHub Actions. Dou palestras em encontros de engenharia de plataforma em Lisboa e acompanho duas pessoas juniores que estão a fazer a transição de desenvolvimento para infraestrutura.

bullets: Operação de clusters EKS partilhados por 18 equipas, com políticas de rede e quotas por equipa.
Defino toda a infraestrutura em Pulumi com TypeScript e revisão obrigatória por pull request.
Implementei fluxos GitOps com Flux; o tempo médio entre merge e produção caiu para 12 minutos.
Lançamento de um portal interno em Backstage, com modelos para novos serviços.
Criação de um catálogo de serviços com informação de responsáveis, o que acelerou a resposta a incidentes.
Introdução de verificação de segurança e assinatura de imagens em todos os fluxos de entrega.
Mantenho documentação, tutoriais e um registo de alterações da plataforma, revistos com as equipas todos os trimestres.
Organizo sessões quinzenais de dúvidas em que as equipas apresentam problemas e decido o que automatizar a seguir.
Migração de aplicações de servidores dedicados para contentores na cloud.
Criação de pipelines GitHub Actions para build, testes e publicação de imagens.
Configuração de dashboards e alertas no Datadog.
Medição de custos por serviço com relatórios semanais enviados às equipas.
Redução de 30% nos custos de computação com redimensionamento e instâncias spot.
Participei em revisões de arquitetura e ajudei a escolher serviços geridos em vez de componentes alojados internamente.

name: Tiago Vasconcelos Peixoto
headline: Engenheiro SRE
summary: Engenheiro SRE com dez anos de carreira, atualmente responsável pela fiabilidade de uma plataforma de comércio eletrónico. Uso Kubernetes, Terraform e CI/CD no dia a dia e dou muita importância a SLOs, observabilidade e análises pós-incidente sem culpa. Fora do trabalho dou formação em fiabilidade a equipas de desenvolvimento e escrevo no blogue interno sobre incidentes que correram mal e o que aprendemos com eles.

bullets: Definição de SLOs para 30 serviços e criação de relatórios mensais de fiabilidade.
Gestão de clusters Kubernetes em duas regiões, descritos em Terraform.
Evolução da plataforma de CI/CD usada por 60 programadores, com deploys progressivos e rollback automático.
Coordenação de resposta a incidentes e formação de novos elementos da escala.
Introdução de testes de carga antes das campanhas, o que evitou uma falha de base de dados na Black Friday.
Redução do volume de alertas em 50% através da consolidação de regras baseadas em sintomas.
Realizo revisões trimestrais de capacidade com as equipas de produto, com base em tendências de utilização e previsões de crescimento.
Mantenho livros de procedimentos para os dez incidentes mais frequentes e atualizo-os depois de cada análise pós-incidente.
Automatização de deploys e monitorização de aplicações web.
Introdução de Docker e de ambientes de teste temporários.
Suporte a produção em regime de piquete.
Criação de um painel com métricas de entrega: frequência de deploys, taxa de falhas e tempo de recuperação.
Formação de dez programadores para operarem os seus próprios serviços.
Participei em exercícios de recuperação de desastres e na migração de bases de dados entre centros de dados.
Administração de servidores Linux e bases de dados MySQL.
Aprendizagem de otimização de MySQL e Linux em grande escala.

name: Rosário Canelas Teodoro
headline: Engenheira Cloud
summary: Engenheira cloud com cinco anos de experiência em Azure. Desenho ambientes seguros e económicos e automatizo a sua criação com Terraform. Também apoio equipas com Kubernetes e pipelines de CI/CD. Gosto de partilhar o que aprendo em sessões internas. Gosto de trabalhar com equipas de segurança e de finanças para equilibrar controlo e velocidade, e participo em encontros de comunidade cloud em Coimbra.

bullets: Defini a estrutura de subscrições e redes em Azure e descrevi-a em módulos Terraform reutilizáveis.
Gestão de um cluster Kubernetes para aplicações de análise de consumos.
Evolução das pipelines de CI/CD no Azure DevOps, com análise de vulnerabilidades em cada build.
Redução de 20% nos custos mensais com ajuste de dimensionamento e desligamento automático de ambientes de teste.
Implementação de endpoints privados e de gestão de identidades para eliminar credenciais em código.
Elaboração de relatórios mensais de conformidade e custos para a direção.
Revejo notas de versão antes de cada atualização do cluster e testo as alterações num ambiente de pré-produção.
Colaboro com equipas de programação para acelerar os lançamentos e simplificar os ambientes de teste.
Participo em reuniões semanais com a equipa de aplicações para planear mudanças e avaliar riscos antes de cada entrega.
Migração de 25 máquinas virtuais para a cloud.
Manutenção de servidores Windows e Linux de clientes.
Elaboração de documentação técnica e procedimentos de recuperação.
Criação de um guia de migração com mapeamento de dependências e plano de reversão.
Formação da equipa de suporte sobre alertas e procedimentos de resposta.
Participei em intervenções de fim de semana com colegas mais experientes e aprendi a fazer reversões seguras.

name: Winston Abernethy-Cole
headline: Senior Systems Administrator
summary: Systems administrator with eighteen years looking after Windows and Linux servers for mid-sized organisations. Reliable, calm during outages and thorough with documentation. I prefer well-tested backups over clever tricks. Outside work I coach a youth football team and restore old radios, which probably explains my patience with legacy hardware. I mentor apprentices and enjoy sharing practical lessons from years of keeping services running.

bullets: Run 140 virtual servers on VMware with replication to a secondary site; tested recovery twice a year.
Administer Active Directory, Group Policy and Exchange for 1,100 staff.
Lead patching cycles and maintain a change calendar approved by the service desk.
Replaced tape backups with Veeam, shortening restore times from hours to minutes.
Documented every system in a configuration database, including owners, dependencies and recovery priorities.
Migrated mailboxes from on-premises Exchange to a hosted mail service over four weekends with no lost messages.
Chair the monthly change meeting, review risks and rollback plans, and keep the business informed of planned outages.
Negotiate hardware and support renewals with suppliers and maintain a lifecycle plan covering servers, storage and network.
Maintained file servers, print servers and Linux web servers.
Managed firewall rules and VPN access for remote workers.
Built a patching schedule that reduced the number of emergency fixes by around a third.
Introduced a clear asset register and hardware refresh plan.
Ran disaster recovery tests with business owners and documented the lessons learned for management.
Desktop support and hardware repairs for 80 users.
Learned the foundations of support, including hardware, networks and printers.

name: Ngozi Eze-Hartmann
headline: IT Administrator
summary: IT administrator for a logistics company with several warehouses. I handle servers, networks, user accounts and, when needed, a screwdriver. Strong on backups, patching and keeping people productive. I work well with warehouse supervisors, drivers and managers alike, and I enjoy translating technical constraints into plain language. In my spare time I volunteer teaching basic IT skills at a community centre.

bullets: Administer 25 servers, two Hyper-V clusters and network equipment across four sites.
Introduced nightly offsite backups with Acronis and quarterly restore drills.
Manage Microsoft 365 licences, mailboxes and multi-factor authentication for 380 users.
Set up warehouse Wi-Fi and barcode scanner connectivity; downtime on scanning fell by more than half.
Replaced ageing switches in two warehouses and documented the cabling, which cut fault-finding time.
Implemented a simple ticketing system and published response targets for the business.
Coordinate with external suppliers for internet lines, telephony and printers, and keep contract renewals on a shared calendar.
Document network layouts, server roles and passwords in a secured vault so that cover during holidays is straightforward.
Run monthly patching on Saturdays outside peak dispatch times.
Evaluate small tools for inventory and remote support and recommend the best value option to management.
First- and second-line support for 150 users.
Maintained printers, thin clients and telephony.
Wrote PowerShell scripts for account creation.
Wrote an onboarding guide for new starters and a short cyber-awareness session for staff.
Standardised workstation images to speed up replacements.
Introduced a standard laptop image and a simple hardware loan pool for new employees.
Handled user questions politely in German and English at all four sites.

name: Piotr Zalewski
headline: Network and Systems Administrator
summary: Administrator with a networking background. I enjoy tidy racks, accurate diagrams and predictable maintenance windows. Eleven years supporting infrastructure in education and public sector. I like documenting networks and keeping maintenance windows predictable. I also teach a short evening course on Linux administration for local adults retraining in IT.

bullets: Manage the campus network of 90 switches and 300 access points.
Run a Proxmox cluster hosting 60 virtual machines and keep Bacula backups to disk and tape.
Operate authentication with OpenLDAP and RADIUS for students and staff.
Keep Zabbix monitoring and an up-to-date network diagram.
Planned and executed a campus-wide VLAN redesign that improved isolation between student, staff and guest traffic.
Introduced a change calendar and a post-maintenance review for each major activity.
Write procedures for network changes, rollbacks and fault escalation, and train the two junior technicians to follow them.
Evaluate new equipment and prepare technical specifications for public tenders, including support and warranty terms.
Maintain a small lab to test firmware upgrades before they reach production switches.
Provide on-call cover for the network during exam periods, when availability matters most to students and lecturers.
Report monthly on bandwidth use, uptime and outstanding tickets to the IT director.
Supported 200 workstations and local servers.
Configured VPN and mail relays.
Built a monitoring dashboard on wall screens in the IT office so problems are visible as they happen.
Implemented 802.1X authentication across wired ports.
Replaced an ageing mail relay with a better-filtered setup and improved spam handling.
Kept an inventory of workstations, licences and warranties for audit purposes.

name: Deepak Ranganathan
headline: Systems Administrator
summary: Systems administrator with six years of experience handling servers, backups and user support in a manufacturing group. I like checklists, clear tickets and doing the dull things properly. I enjoy working directly with plant managers to understand which systems matter most to production and plan maintenance around shifts. I am studying for a cloud fundamentals certification in my evenings.

bullets: Look after 45 servers across two plants; maintain 99% availability for production planning systems.
Patch servers monthly using SCCM and a documented rollback plan.
Support Active Directory, shared drives and printing for 600 users.
Review backup reports daily and perform quarterly restore tests.
Prepared and tested a disaster recovery plan for the production planning database, with recovery in under two hours.
Replaced an ageing firewall pair with a managed high-availability setup, with a planned cutover at a weekend.
Coordinate maintenance windows with production supervisors so that updates happen during planned stoppages.
Monitor server health, disk growth and backup success using Zabbix dashboards and daily checks.
Manage user accounts, mailbox quotas and permissions through documented request and approval steps.
Prepare monthly availability and incident reports for the plant IT manager and track improvement actions to closure.
Resolved desktop and server tickets for several clients.
Installed and configured firewalls and switches during office moves.
Learned scripting and wrote a few small PowerShell tools to report on stale accounts and disk usage.
Documented network diagrams for both plants.
Replaced faulty hardware, reinstalled operating systems and supported users by phone and remote tools.
Kept a simple knowledge base of fixes that colleagues could follow.

certifications: Microsoft Certified: Windows Server Hybrid Administrator

name: Bronagh McAlinden
headline: Head of IT Operations
summary: Twenty-two years in IT operations, starting on the service desk and now managing a small team that runs infrastructure for a law firm. Hands-on when needed, focused on continuity, security and good relationships with the business. I enjoy building teams and mentoring people who are starting out in IT; two of my former service desk staff are now senior engineers. I sit on the firm's risk committee as the technology representative.

bullets: Manage a team of four administrators and an outsourced security provider.
Led a data centre exit to a colocation facility and a refreshed virtual environment, completed over a weekend with no data loss.
Own the disaster recovery plan, tested annually with partners.
Achieved Cyber Essentials Plus certification for three consecutive years.
Managed an annual budget of 1.4 million pounds and negotiated vendor contracts that saved 12% year on year.
Introduced a clear incident and change process aligned with ITIL, cutting repeat incidents by a third.
Report quarterly to the partners on availability, incidents, security posture and project progress.
Select and manage managed-service partners, with clear service levels and regular reviews.
Administered servers, email and point-of-sale back-office systems.
Introduced centralised patching and imaging for 300 PCs.
Planned and led a major email platform migration for 900 users with minimal disruption.
Wrote the firm's information security policies and ran awareness training.
Supervised a team of six on the helpdesk and server support, with weekly coaching sessions.
Handled 40 tickets a day and escalated server issues.
Learned how a service desk works in a large public body, including escalation and customer care.

name: Henrik Strandberg
headline: Linux Systems Administrator
summary: Linux administrator, thirteen years. I keep mail, web and database servers running for a hosting provider and enjoy scripting my way out of repetitive work. Keen on security hardening and clean documentation. Outside work I tinker with old computers, brew beer and take part in a local amateur radio club. I enjoy mentoring new technicians and write short guides for the support team.

bullets: Administer 250 physical and virtual servers hosting 9,000 customer sites.
Run mail infrastructure handling 2 million messages a day, with spam filtering and blacklist monitoring.
Tune MariaDB replicas and schedule consistent backups verified weekly.
Wrote Bash and Perl tools for account provisioning that saved support about 15 hours a week.
Hardened servers against brute-force attacks with fail2ban, key-only logins and automated updates.
Managed a migration of 1,500 websites between data centres in a single month with minimal downtime.
Provide third-line support to the customer care team and work through complex mail delivery and database performance cases.
Take part in an on-call rota every sixth week and write post-incident summaries.
Run quarterly restore tests on randomly chosen customer accounts and record the results.
Contribute to hiring by interviewing candidates for technician roles and preparing practical Linux troubleshooting exercises.
Keep configuration files under version control with Git and review changes with a colleague before deployment.
Maintained Linux servers and desktop support for office staff.
Documented server builds and recovery steps in a wiki used by the whole team.
Handled server installs, cabling and rack work in the data centre.
Set up the first centralised log server for the support team.

name: Aurélio Bettencourt Maia
headline: Administrador de Sistemas
summary: Administrador de sistemas com catorze anos de experiência em ambientes Windows e Linux. Cuido de servidores, redes, backups e apoio a utilizadores numa empresa do setor hoteleiro. Valorizo a estabilidade, os procedimentos escritos e a comunicação clara com a gestão. Fora do trabalho sou voluntário numa associação local de apoio informático a idosos e gosto de ensinar utilizadores a protegerem-se de fraudes e de phishing.

bullets: Administração de 35 servidores virtuais e da rede de seis unidades hoteleiras.
Implementação de cópias de segurança com Veeam e testes de recuperação trimestrais.
Gestão de contas, correio e autenticação multifator para 700 colaboradores.
Coordenação de intervenções fora de horas para não afetar a reserva de quartos.
Substituição de equipamento de rede em todas as unidades, com documentação atualizada e esquemas de cablagem.
Implementação de um sistema de pedidos de suporte com tempos de resposta definidos.
Coordeno fornecedores de ligações à Internet, telefones e impressoras e mantenho um calendário de renovações de contratos.
Documento a rede, as funções de cada servidor e as credenciais de emergência num cofre protegido.
Realizo a aplicação mensal de atualizações aos sábados, fora dos períodos de maior ocupação.
Suporte a postos de trabalho e servidores de ficheiros.
Configuração de firewalls e ligações VPN entre lojas.
Gestão de inventário de equipamento.
Formação de colegas sobre segurança, palavras-passe e boas práticas no uso do correio eletrónico.
Elaboração do orçamento anual de equipamento informático.
Introdução de uma imagem padrão para portáteis e de um processo simples para novos colaboradores.

certifications: Microsoft Certified: Windows Server Hybrid Administrator

name: Gisela Pimenta Cardoso
headline: Técnica de Sistemas e Redes
summary: Técnica de sistemas e redes com quatro anos de experiência numa autarquia. Faço manutenção de servidores, gestão de utilizadores e apoio técnico. Sou organizada, aprendo depressa e gosto de deixar tudo documentado para quem vier a seguir. Estou a preparar-me para a certificação de Linux e participo em formações da autarquia sobre cibersegurança e proteção de dados.

bullets: Administração de 15 servidores e da rede de dez edifícios municipais.
Gestão de utilizadores, permissões e correio eletrónico para 450 pessoas.
Reformulação do plano de cópias de segurança, com cópia externa semanal.
Monitorização com Zabbix e abertura de pedidos a fornecedores.
Criação de um inventário de equipamentos e licenças que ajudou a planear renovações.
Apoio à implementação de autenticação multifator no correio eletrónico dos serviços municipais.
Acompanho fornecedores externos na manutenção de equipamentos e confirmo que as intervenções ficam bem registadas.
Mantenho documentação de rede, listas de contactos e procedimentos de emergência para quem estiver de serviço.
Realizo atualizações mensais de sistemas em horário acordado com os serviços.
Apoio a clientes empresariais em instalação de postos de trabalho.
Substituição de equipamento de rede e configuração de Wi-Fi.
Registo de intervenções num sistema de tickets.
Elaboração de guias rápidos para os utilizadores e de uma lista de verificação para novas contas.
Participação em ações de formação em cibersegurança.
Atendimento por telefone e presencial a utilizadores com dúvidas sobre computadores, impressoras e correio eletrónico.
Aprendizagem de boas práticas de segurança e de gestão de contas.
